column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
A family wants to buy a house in five years. What kinds of money decisions must they make from now?
Which pillar comes first, and why can none of the others work without it?
How can writing down a plan stop a family from overspending on things they do not really need?
To buy a ₹3,000 bicycle in six months, how much goes aside each month, and what should you do if bus fares suddenly rise?
Why would a family set aside money even in a month when nothing seems to be needed?
Priya's money stayed ₹500 for a year while Sameer's grew. Why might her ₹500 buy less than before?
After the first year's interest is added, what exactly earns interest in the second year?
Two friends save equally every year but one starts ten years later. Who ends up with more at the finish, and why does the gap look so big?
Which two options would suit someone who cannot afford any surprises in their income, and why?
Why might someone without time or experience prefer a managed pool over picking individual company stakes?
A family needs money for a wedding in two years. Which of the four things must they think about first?
Is the choice that promises the biggest payoff automatically the best one for every person? What else should be weighed?
Why does a small payment every month from many people let a few of them recover from a very large loss?
A farmer's harvest is destroyed by flood and the family's earner falls ill in the same year. Which kinds of cover would matter?
Two people each take a loan of the same size: one to study, one to buy a gadget they barely need. How do their futures differ?
A family pays for an appliance in twelve equal monthly payments. What two things does each payment cover?
When you buy a notebook, which kind of tax is hidden in the price, and which kind do salaried workers pay on what they earn?
Why might a system ask people earning more to give a larger share, and what does the whole society gain?
Who decides the ranges and rates each year, and which body looks after direct tax laws?
Walk through the steps from a yearly salary to a final tax figure; what is subtracted first, and how are the portions combined?
